title: [IELTS Trainer] - Petrol expenditure across income groups in the US and the UK
prompt: The graph below gives information about how much people in the United States and the United Kingdom spend on petrol. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph compares the proportion of income that drivers in the United States and the United Kingdom spend on petrol across different income groups.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there are contrasting trends between the two countries. In the US, poorer households spend a higher percentage of their income on petrol, while in the UK, wealthier individuals allocate more of their income to fuel costs.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the United States, the poorest group spends between 3.7% and 4.8% of their income on petrol, which is the highest proportion among all groups. This figure then decreases for middle-income earners to around 3.8-4.8%, before dropping further for the richest group to approximately 2.3-3.8%. This shows that petrol expenditure represents a greater financial burden for lower-income Americans.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, the United Kingdom shows an opposite pattern. The poorest drivers spend only a small fraction of their income on petrol, ranging from 0.4% to 2.5%. This rises steadily for middle-income households to between 2.5% and 3.8%, and continues to increase for the wealthiest group, reaching 3.3-3.8%. This indicates that higher earners in the UK spend proportionally more of their income on fuel.
